root_cause.text: In wlcore's `wl1271_op_resume()` resume path, the function could jump to cleanup and `mutex_unlock(&wl->mutex)` before `wl->mutex` was ever acquired because the mutex lock was placed after `pm_runtime_force_resume()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `mutex_lock(&wl->mutex);` from below the `wl_lock`/IRQ section to immediately before `pm_runtime_force_resume(wl->dev);`, and the commit message explicitly says to “Make sure that wl->mutex is locked before it is unlocked.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Acquire the driver mutex before forcing runtime resume to protect the resume path from concurrent access races.
intent_record.what: A call to mutex_lock(&wl->mutex) was added in wl1271_op_resume() immediately before invoking pm_runtime_force_resume(wl->dev).
intent_record.how: This change ensures the driver's mutex is held during the resume path before forcing the device runtime resume, serializing access to shared driver state and preventing concurrent operations from racing with resume handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary mutex acquisition in wl1271_op_resume() to fix incorrect locking during the resume path.
intent_record.what: The call to mutex_lock(&wl->mutex); was removed from wl1271_op_resume() immediately before the recovery-flag check and subsequent SDIO-related logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, wl1271_op_resume() no longer acquires wl->mutex at that point, which avoids taking that mutex during resume in this path and changes the locking behavior for the recovery check and following operations.

candidates.rationale: The resume path invoked force_resume before acquiring wl->mutex, making later error handling able to reach cleanup that unlocks an unheld mutex and leaving the path unprotected from concurrent access.

This lock acquisition occurred too late in the function, after pm_runtime_force_resume(), which is the core ordering bug that allowed cleanup to unlock wl->mutex before it had been acquired on earlier error paths.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call was executed before wl->mutex was acquired, creating the vulnerable ordering in wl1271_op_resume(). If an error path after this point jumped to cleanup, the function could reach mutex_unlock(&wl->mutex) even though the mutex had not yet been locked.

This mutex acquisition occurred too late in the resume path, after pm_runtime_force_resume(). Its placement is part of the root cause because earlier failures could reach cleanup and unlock an unheld mutex, and the path remained unprotected from concurrent access until this point.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 725b82775e7901dc92afaddfa45683934e75c33e
Author: Arik Nemtsov <arik@wizery.com>
Date:   Thu Jun 21 18:10:52 2012 +0300

    wlcore: prevent recovery in the middle of resume
    
    Take the mutex early in the resume handler and use the locked version of
    the IRQ routine. This ensures any recoveries queued will only take place
    after resume has fully completed.
    
    Signed-off-by: Arik Nemtsov <arik@wizery.com>
    Signed-off-by: Luciano Coelho <coelho@ti.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the ordering inside `wl1271_op_resume()`. The root cause was that resume could reach cleanup and `mutex_unlock(&wl->mutex)` before the mutex had been acquired, because `mutex_lock(&wl->mutex)` was placed after `pm_runtime_force_resume()`. In this commit version, the function now acquires the mutex early: `mutex_lock(&wl->mutex);` is added before the recovery/IRQ handling block and before the old later lock location. The old late lock is explicitly removed (`- mutex_lock(&wl->mutex);`). This demonstrates the fix is present: the mutex is taken earlier in the resume path, preventing an unlock-before-lock situation on error/cleanup paths after resume processing begins. The additional change from `wlcore_irq(0, wl);` to `ret = wlcore_irq_locked(wl); if (ret) wl12xx_queue_recovery_work(wl);` is consistent with the commit message about using the locked IRQ routine while the mutex is held. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is already applied.
